modelo210_en:
Own a home in Spain that stands empty most of the year? Spain still expects a tax return for it.
Modelo 210 applies to non-residents even when the property earns nothing. The tax is based on the cadastral value, not the market price, so the amount is usually smaller than people fear. Miss it for years and the arrears often surface when you sell. A calendar reminder in early December solves most of it.

buying_fees_en:
The asking price is never the real price in Spain.
Plan for 12-14% on top before you fall in love with a listing. Transfer tax varies by region, so the same home can cost thousands more a few kilometres away. New builds work differently, with 10% VAT instead. The fees fall due right around completion, so keep that money liquid, not invested. Ask for a full cost breakdown before you sign anything.

scams_en:
If a Spanish property deal feels rushed, that is the biggest red flag of all.
Before any money moves, order a Nota Simple to confirm who really owns the home. If payment details suddenly change by email, call the agency on the number from their official website, never the one in the message. And ask for the tourist licence number, then check it in the regional registry yourself. Honest sellers never mind the extra day.

owners_year_en:
Spanish property bills do not arrive all at once. They arrive all year.
IBI lands between May and October, and the bill often only goes to a Spanish address. Community fees tick along monthly or quarterly. The non-resident tax return closes the year on 31 December. Set up direct debits for the recurring ones and keep a simple annual calendar. Most surprises are really just missed post.

I den perioden kan politiet ofte fjerne inntrengere raskt. Etterpå må saken gjennom retten, og det kan ta halvannet til to år. Gjør derfor boligen lite attraktiv: lys med tidsur, alarm og naboer som sier ifra. Det finnes egne forsikringer mot okkupasjon. Og bytt aldri låsen selv mens noen bor der, det kan gi deg problemer med loven.

ibi_sv:
Har du sett årets IBI-räkning? Många fastighetsägare har aldrig fått den i handen.
Räkningarna skickas ofta bara inom Spanien, så äger du på distans är autogiro hos kommunen den enklaste lösningen. Skatten ligger på 0,3-1,1 % av taxeringsvärdet och varierar mellan kommuner. Viktigast av allt: obetald IBI följer fastigheten, inte ägaren. Kontrollera därför alltid en Nota Simple innan du köper.

nie_application_en:
You cannot buy a home in Spain without one small piece of paper.
The NIE number itself never expires, but for property purchases the certificate is often only accepted for three months, so time your application. Pay the small fee at a bank first using form 790 and bring the stamped proof. Queues can close around 13:30, so go early. In busy areas, book the appointment online weeks ahead.

sepa_swift_en:
Sending money to Spain the wrong way costs you at every step.
SWIFT transfers can pass through several intermediary banks, and each one may take a slice. SEPA needs nothing more than an IBAN and moves euros quickly at little or no cost. One catch: many Spanish utilities and town halls still want a Spanish account for direct debits. Send euros, not your home currency, and let SEPA carry them.

community_fees_en:
Community fees are the running cost new owners underestimate most.
They pay for lifts, pools, gardens and the building itself, and they range from modest to serious money. Before buying, ask for a certificate showing the seller owes nothing, because part of old debt can pass to you. And go to the annual meeting or send a proxy. That is where fee rises and big works are decided.
Save this for later. More at 247spain.es
#SpainProperty #SpanishHomeOwners #LivingInSpain #CommunityFees #BuyingInSpain
solar_energy_en:
Solar panels in Spain pay for themselves faster than most people expect.
With 300 or more sunny days a year, bills can drop sharply, and the old sun tax disappeared back in 2019. One detail surprises many owners: without a battery, panels shut off in a power cut for safety. Also worth checking, many town halls offer IBI discounts for homes with solar. Ask before you install.

holiday_home_cost_en:
What does a holiday home in Spain cost in the months you are not there?
For a typical apartment, plan on a few hundred euros monthly, and roughly double for a villa with pool and garden. Add key holding and an alarm and €400-500 is realistic. The useful trick is to budget yearly, not monthly, because IBI and insurance land as single large bills. An empty home still works quietly through your account.

#SpainProperty #HolidayHome #SpanishHomeOwners #LivingInSpain #MoveToSpain
buying_10_steps_en:
The arras contract is the moment a Spanish purchase turns serious.
Walk away after signing and you lose your 10% deposit. If the seller walks, they owe you double. That symmetry is why the arras matters more than the offer itself. If you need a mortgage, the FEIN offer starts a mandatory 10-day reflection period, so build it into your timeline. Never sign arras before the legal checks are done.
Save this for later. More at 247spain.es
#SpainProperty #BuyingInSpain #MoveToSpain #LivingInSpain #SpanishHomeOwners
nota_simple_en:
The cheapest document in a Spanish property purchase can save you the most money.
A Nota Simple shows the registered owner, mortgages, embargoes and debts, and in Spain those debts travel with the home, not the seller. You can order it yourself from the Land Registry for around ten euros online, no agent needed. One tip: order a fresh copy right before signing too. Things can change between viewing and completion.
Save this for later. More at 247spain.es
#SpainProperty #NotaSimple #BuyingInSpain #MoveToSpain #LivingInSpain
plusvalia_en:
Buying from a non-resident seller in Spain quietly changes who pays what.
As the buyer, you withhold 3% of the price and pay it straight to the tax office on the seller's behalf. Plusvalía, the municipal tax on land value gains, is filed by you when the seller lives abroad, paid from money withheld from the seller, with 30 days to reach the council. Agree in writing before completion who handles each payment. It saves arguments later.
Save this for later. More at 247spain.es
General information, not tax advice.

rental_rule_changes_en:
Renting out your Spanish home short term? The rules changed in 2025.
Every rental property now needs its own registration number, and it must appear on the advert. Platforms are removing listings without one, and the code has to be renewed every 12 months, so set a reminder. Check your community statutes too. Some buildings have voted to ban tourist lets entirely, and that vote binds you.

#SpainProperty #HolidayRental #SpanishHomeOwners #LivingInSpain #MoveToSpain
epc_certificates_en:
You can be fined for a Spanish property advert before anyone even views the home.
The energy certificate is required at the advertising stage, not just at the sale. Getting one is simple: a technician visits, and the certificate then stays valid for ten years. A decent rating can even support your asking price. Make sure the certificate is registered with your region, an unregistered one does not count.
Save this for later. More at 247spain.es
#SpainProperty #EPC #SpanishHomeOwners #LivingInSpain #SellingInSpain
buyer_visas_en:
Buying a home in Spain no longer buys you the right to stay.
The golden visa is closed to new applicants, so a purchase and a residence permit are now separate questions. The non-lucrative visa needs passive income of about €28,000 a year and does not allow work. The digital nomad visa suits remote workers earning around €2,500 a month. No visa? The 90/180 rule still gives generous part-time use. Count your days carefully.
Save this for later. More at 247spain.es
#SpainProperty #MoveToSpain #SpainVisa #LivingInSpain #RetireInSpain
citizenship_en:
Marrying a Spaniard does not hand you a Spanish passport.
The standard route is ten years of continuous legal residence. Marriage shortens that to one year, but only if you actually live in Spain as a resident. Everyone sits two exams: the CCSE culture test and the DELE A2 Spanish exam. And check the dual citizenship rules for your nationality first. For many, taking the Spanish passport means formally giving up the old one.

#LivingInSpain #MoveToSpain #SpanishCitizenship #SpainProperty #ExpatSpain
retiring_spain_en:
Retiring to Spain costs less than many expect. The paperwork decides everything else.
Spend more than 183 days a year there and you become tax resident, with worldwide income, pensions included, taxed in Spain. Double tax treaties usually stop the same income being taxed twice, but the filing still has to happen. The visa route asks for proof of funds and private health cover without co-payments. Outside the big cities, €18,000-27,000 a year buys a comfortable life.

property_insurance_en:
Home insurance is not legally required in Spain. Skipping it is still a bad idea.
If you have a mortgage, the bank will insist on it anyway. Know the difference between building cover and contents cover, and check what your community's block policy already includes so you do not pay twice. One detail matters for holiday homes: many standard policies limit payouts if the home sits empty for months. Ask specifically about vacant-home cover.
Save this for later. More at 247spain.es
#SpainProperty #SpanishHomeOwners #HolidayHome #LivingInSpain #HomeInsurance
direct_debit_en:
In Spain, the company decides when your bill leaves your account. Not you.
Direct debits run on a signed SEPA mandate with your IBAN, and each provider picks its own collection date. When you switch banks, nothing moves across automatically. You have to give the new IBAN to every single provider. Keep a buffer in the account too. A bounced debit can mean return fees and, eventually, cut services.
Save this for later. More at 247spain.es
#SpainProperty #LivingInSpain #BankingInSpain #SpanishHomeOwners #MoveToSpain
frozen_account_en:
A Spanish bank account can be blocked while you are 2,000 km away.
The warning letters usually arrive by post, in Spanish, at your Spanish address, which is why so many owners never see them. An expired passport is the most common cause and is fixed within days by sending updated documents. Unpaid IBI or taxes are the more serious trigger. Give your bank an email address and have someone check the mailbox.
Save this for later. More at 247spain.es
#SpainProperty #BankingInSpain #SpanishHomeOwners #LivingInSpain #HolidayHome
buying_documents_en:
In Spain you do not just buy the property. You buy everything owed on it.
Unpaid IBI, community fees and mortgages stay attached to the home, which is why the Nota Simple, around €10 online, is the first document to order. The NIE fee is paid at a bank with form 790 before your appointment, so bring the stamped form. Non-EU citizens, including Brits, should start the NIE early. It takes longer now.
Save this for later. More at 247spain.es
#SpainProperty #BuyingInSpain #MoveToSpain #NIE #NotaSimple
offer_accepted_en:
An accepted offer in Spain means less than you think.
Until the arras contract is signed, nothing is binding and the seller can still take a better offer. The arras changes everything: pull out and you lose the 10% deposit, but if the seller quits, they pay you double. From there, expect six to ten weeks to keys. Get your NIE, bank account and funds ready before you bid, not after.
Save this for later. More at 247spain.es
#SpainProperty #BuyingInSpain #MoveToSpain #LivingInSpain #SpanishHomeOwners
late_tax_penalties_en:
Missed a Spanish tax deadline? Moving first is worth real money.
If you file voluntarily before any letter arrives, the surcharges stay small and grow slowly month by month. Wait until the tax office contacts you and proper penalties apply instead. The non-resident tax runs on its own quiet schedule, due by 31 December the following year, which is exactly why so many owners miss it. Catching up is usually straightforward.

Det lureste er å budsjettere per år, ikke per måned, siden IBI og forsikring kommer som store enkeltregninger. En tom bolig jobber stille videre på kontoen din.

I Spanien köper du inte bara fastigheten. Du köper allt som är skyldigt på den.
Obetald IBI, föreningsavgifter och lån följer med huset, och därför är en Nota Simple för under €4 det första dokumentet att beställa. NIE-avgiften på cirka €12 betalas på bank med blankett 790 innan ditt besök, så ta med den stämplade blanketten. Medborgare utanför EU får räkna med längre väntetid. Börja i god tid.
Spara det här till senare. Mer på 247spain.es

modelo210_sv:
Står din fastighet i Spanien tom större delen av året? Spanien vill ändå ha en deklaration.
Modelo 210 gäller alla fastighetsägare som inte bor i Spanien, även utan hyresintäkter. Skatten räknas på taxeringsvärdet, inte marknadspriset, så beloppet är ofta lägre än man befarar. Sista dag är den 31 december året efter. Hyr du ut redovisar du i stället kvartalsvis. En påminnelse i början av december räcker långt.
Spara det här till senare. Mer på 247spain.es

scams_sv:
Känns den spanska bostadsannonsen för bra för att vara sann? Då är den oftast just det.
Innan några pengar rör sig, beställ en Nota Simple och kontrollera vem som verkligen äger fastigheten. Ändras kontonumret plötsligt via mejl, ring mäklaren på numret från den officiella webbplatsen, aldrig det i meddelandet. Be om numret på turistlicensen och slå upp det själv i regionens register. Tidspress är i sig en varningssignal.
